name: MS Biomedical Engineering
notes: Fully online, no residency; flat $745 per credit with no added fees. Lowest price in the scan. Delivered through UH-Extend. Admission expects calculus, differential equations, linear algebra and a STEM bachelor's; leveling courses available. Enrollment not published. Focus per scan: imaging, neural and rehab engineering, bionanoscience.

name: MEng, Biomedical Engineering specialization
notes: Online or on campus, coursework only. Total is the scan's own arithmetic (about $28,920). The $964 per credit comes from a CSU-sponsored post, not a bursar page, so treat as indicative. Focus per scan: biomechanics, tissue and materials.

name: MS Biomedical Engineering (Weldon)
notes: Fully online, self-paced by course, 5-year limit. Cost shown is the resident table; the higher tier is $43,770 ($1,459 per credit). 12 of 30 credits come from a regulatory and professional list (design controls, quality systems, human factors, ethics, entrepreneurship). Sample plan has no capstone. A 9-credit regulatory affairs certificate stacks into the degree. Closest program to what BU would build. Enrollment not published. Courses: 10 is the sum of the listed components (2 BME technical, 1 quantitative, 1 life-sciences, 4 regulatory/professional, 2 electives).

name: MS/MSE Interdisciplinary Engineering, BME concentration
notes: Fully online. 18+ of 30 credits in engineering. Scan describes a lighter BME core with 18 elective credits. Cost is the same table as the Weldon MS (higher tier $43,770). Can pair with Purdue's online MBA.

name: MS Biomedical Engineering
notes: 100% online; course-only or project option. $39,000 is after the tuition reduction; alumni get $3,900 more off. Per-credit rate listed as n/a. Only confirmed OPM relationship in the scan (Everspring). Translational layer includes regulatory aspects of health technology, biodesign, engineering management; capstone ties to medical device design. Admissions run through Spring 2027 per second pass. Courses: 10 is the sum of the listed components (4 BME, 2 core engineering, 2 translational, 2 technical electives).

name: MEng Bioengineering (MAGE)
notes: Online or campus, non-thesis, not I-20 eligible. Ten courses. Format is linked (catalog URL shown); the $1,567 online rate (vs $1,271 standard on-campus) is second pass, and total is the scan's arithmetic. Same rate for residents and non-residents. A secondary directory lists courses in regulatory affairs, device development, biosensors, image analysis and machine learning; not confirmed on UMD pages. MAGE says bioengineering is not among its five largest areas, suggesting it is small.

name: MS Applied Biomedical Engineering
notes: Ten courses (credits not stated), 5-year limit. $5,620 per course after the dean's fellowship. Online or on-site, but a required residency includes two lab weekends in Baltimore, the only working model found for hands-on content in an online BME degree. Focus areas per scan: imaging, medical devices, neuroengineering, translational tissue engineering, plus a general area. Course list includes Regulation of Medical Devices and Rehabilitation Engineering. Provisional admission allowed.

name: MS Biomedical Engineering
notes: Fully online via DEN; thesis optional (4 units). 28 units: 17 required, at least 11 elective. Total is the scan's arithmetic, before fees; $2,742 per unit is the same online and on campus. General BME. USC keeps its Medical Device and Diagnostic Engineering MS off DEN and its imaging informatics MS is not currently available.

name: MS Biomedical Engineering
notes: Fully online, part-time, 5-year limit, no transfer credit; 30 points. $88,715 is a CVN estimate; $2,822 per credit plus $395 per course. Required computational modeling of physiological systems course; no capstone or thesis. Most science-heavy and most expensive program in the set. Courses: 10 is the sum of the listed components (1 required modeling, 2 core, 2 BME electives, 1 applied math, 4 free electives).

name: MS Biomedical Engineering
notes: Department marks it available fully online; thesis (6-credit defense) or non-thesis. Online tuition not published. Focus per scan: biomaterials, biomechanics, imaging, broad electives (biological sciences, biomedical sciences, complex systems and brain sciences, nursing).

name: MEng in AI Engineering, BME concentration
notes: Online and residential; all required courses but one (AI for Experiment Design) are available online, so format is shown as hybrid. 30 credits: 12 AI/ML foundations, 12 at the intersection with biomedicine, 6 knowledge extensions. Cost not fixed (U-M estimator). Timing conflict to check: BME page says Fall 2027 MEng and Winter 2027 certificate; the college release says remote options may start with or after the campus launch. The scan says it covers AI in medicine, not device lifecycle and regulation. Can be fed by Michigan's SUGS sequential-degree program (up to 9 credits double-counted). Scan says AI in medicine but not device lifecycle or regulation; this is an inference from program description, not a verified curriculum claim. Highest-priority cell to re-verify.

name: MS Regulatory Affairs
notes: 100% online; credits are quarter hours; moving to semesters Fall 2026. Tuition is an estimate. Concentrations include Medical Device RA and QA Compliance; capstone; digital health cybersecurity elective. Boston-based, lists Boston Scientific among alumni employers. In BU's own market.

name: MS Regulatory Science
notes: Ten courses / 40 credits at $5,740 per course. Drug and biologics emphasis; practicum. Peterson's lists 156 students, year unstated.

name: MS Regulatory Science
notes: Online or in person, live or recorded; 36 units. Weekend courses for working professionals. Tuition not verified.

name: MS Biomedical Diagnostics
notes: Online, 7.5-week classes. Diagnostics science, business, policy. Tuition not verified.

name: MS Clinical Research Management, Regulatory Science
notes: Listing only; the scan did not read the program page. It is unclear from the scan whether this is one program or two. Tuition and credits not read.

name: MS Artificial Intelligence in Medicine
notes: 100% online; 8 core courses and 2 electives. Run by the Speed School's Bioengineering department with Bioinformatics and Biostatistics. Big data, imaging, biostatistics; no GRE. Tuition not verified. Covers AI in medicine, not device lifecycle and regulation. Courses: 10 is the scan's 8 core plus 2 electives.

name: MS Medical Device Engineering
notes: Online cohort capped at 45, two years, live plus recorded. Device design, biomaterials, production, regulatory. Housed in Mechanical Engineering. Credits and tuition not read.

name: MS Medical Device Innovation (TLI)
notes: About 21 months, flexible for working professionals. Whether it is online is unconfirmed, so format is left blank. Innovation management, regulatory, IP, commercialization. On the scan's confirm-before-external-use list.

name: MEng, clinical engineering plan of study
notes: All courses online, about 3 years. Hospital technology leadership. Tuition not verified.

name: MS Healthcare Systems Engineering
notes: Operations and process improvement, not devices. Credits and tuition not read.

name: MS Industrial Engineering, healthcare systems track
notes: Systems and quality emphasis. Tuition not verified.

name: MS Health Informatics
notes: Online; includes a personal health informatics concentration. Credits and tuition not read.

name: MS Bioengineering
notes: Hybrid; some asynchronous courses, not fully online. 32 semester hours. Campus research-oriented degree. Rests on an aggregator listing only. Tuition not verified; official page needed.

name: MS Artificial Intelligence
notes: Fully online. General AI, not medicine-specific. Credits and tuition not read.

name: MS Artificial Intelligence
notes: Fully online. General AI, not medicine-specific. Credits and tuition not read.

name: Graduate Certificate, Regulatory Affairs for Medical Devices
notes: Resident table price. Stacks into the online MS. The scan row gives no year; 2025-26 is taken from the cited bursar page, which is the same page as the Purdue MS row.

name: Graduate Certificate in Biomedical Engineering
notes: 9 credits. Stacks into the online MS. $6,705 is consistent with the MS's flat $745 per credit, but the scan states the per-credit rate only for the MS.

name: Graduate Certificate, Medical Device Development
notes: Evening classes; online status not confirmed, so format is left blank. Credits apply toward an MS. Tuition not verified.

name: Certificate, Medical Device Engineering
notes: Online, non-degree. Design, manufacturing, quality, regulatory. Tuition not verified.

name: AI in Healthcare certificate
university: Johns Hopkins University (Engineering for Professionals, with Great Learning)
notes: Online, 10 weeks, non-degree. Short course, not a master's. Delivered with Great Learning; the scan does not say what kind of arrangement that is.

name: MS Innovations in Medical and Patient Care Technologies (IMPACT)
notes: Full-time, in person, with Mayo Clinic; built on the Stanford Biodesign process; graduates also earn a 3-credit Mayo clinical innovation certificate. Linked page exists, but program details are second pass.

name: MEng Medical Device Development
notes: First cohort September 2025. Nine months, twelve courses, in person at Aggie Square (Sacramento); three-quarter capstone and clinical shadowing. Linked page exists, but launch details are second pass. City is the UC Davis main campus.

name: MS Medical Device Engineering
notes: Nine months, full time, ending in an industry-sponsored team project.

name: MEng, medical device specialization
notes: Residential MEng with a medical device specialization. The scan gives no further detail.

name: Master of Health Science in Medical Artificial Intelligence
notes: School of Medicine degree: asynchronous lectures plus required in-person bootcamps in New Haven. Open only to residents of the US, Canada and Mexico. Announced, not yet enrolling.

name: MS Artificial Intelligence in Biomedical and Health Sciences
notes: From the College of Medicine. Online status not confirmed, so format is left blank. Described in the scan under announced programs.

name: MS Healthcare Technologies Management
university: Marquette University / Medical College of Wisconsin
notes: Currently not admitting; no evidence of resumed admissions. Cited in the scan as evidence that clinical engineering and healthcare technology management are hard to sustain online. Format not stated in the scan.

name: Online Accelerated Master's (4+)
notes: Penn undergraduates take up to three graduate courses during the bachelor's, then finish about seven courses fully online within three years. Covers only Penn Engineering's existing online master's (computing and data science); bioengineering is not among them. Included as the proof of the finish-remotely model.

name: MS Biomedical Engineering
notes: Checked and not found online. Georgia Tech's online master's are OMSCS, Analytics, Cybersecurity and International Security, plus distance MS programs in aerospace and computational science; the BME MS is campus-only.

name: Joint NC State-UNC BME MS (incl. 11-month MedTech Innovation and Entrepreneurship concentration)
university: North Carolina State University / UNC-Chapel Hill
notes: Checked and not found online. NC State's Engineering Online doesn't carry BME, and the joint BME MS, including its 11-month MedTech concentration, is in person. City shown is NC State's; the program is joint with UNC-Chapel Hill. Second pass; no link in the scan.

name: MS Biomedical Engineering (campus)
notes: Checked and not found online. A three-semester campus program. ASU Online lists an online BSE in BME and an online MS in Biomedical Diagnostics (see that adjacent row), but no online MS in BME.

name: MSE Bioengineering
notes: Checked and not found online in practice. Mixes online and campus courses, but only non-bioengineering courses have online sections, so the core is not online. The scan's example of a hybrid label with no online core.
